statement: European leading-edge foundry demand never existed at the scale assumed in 2022, so no feasible subsidy level would have produced a viable Magdeburg fab.
mechanism: A leading-edge fab needs anchor customers with volumes large enough to fill it. Europe's semiconductor demand is concentrated in automotive and industrial applications that use mature nodes, which is why the contemporaneous Dresden project is built on 28/22 and 16/12 processes rather than leading edge (FACT-002 context). With no European anchor for 18A/14A, the fab's output would have had to be exported into a market where Intel was already losing share. Subsidy reduces the capital cost but not the missing revenue, so the project fails on revenue rather than on financing. Weakest link: the inference that no anchor customer could have been found - this is asserted from absence of evidence, and absence of a retrieved commitment is not proof that none was possible.

relation_to_others.note: Necessary partner: demand sets the option's value
Both explain the cut, but HYP-003 says it would have happened anywhere outside the US anchor base
